gap: No result ChatGPT got says that a dual-screen extender running from one USB-C cable on laptop power alone measured only 160 cd/m², against a 226 cd/m² maximum with its own power adapter (Notebookcheck, X-Rite i1Pro 2, UPERFECT UStation Delta). So 'driver-free, one cable' can cost about 30% of the screen's brightness unless the extender's adapter is plugged in.
standout_why: deskgearhq.com (results 8 and 1 in the two chats, read in full 2026-11-18) gives only maker or listing specs and says itself that independent lab tests of these products are scarce. It has no measured brightness, power or gamut figures and does not mention brightness on laptop power. The answers in both ChatGPT chats give no measured figures; they cite Best Buy, FOPO, Plugable and TUTT product pages. I could not read gradedpicks.com (SSL certificate error) or the FOPO S11 page (HTTP 429). I did not open the Best Buy, Plugable or TUTT pages, which are retail or maker listings. So the claim that no rival has this figure rests on deskgearhq and the ChatGPT answers, not on every result.
decides: It doesn't change which screen wins. The deciding question is still native DP Alt Mode against a display driver, plus how many external displays the laptop can drive. What it changes is the setup advice for a driver-free pick: run on laptop power alone, a single-cable extender can be noticeably dimmer. Notebookcheck measured 160 against 226 cd/m² on the UStation Delta, and Macworld saw the Trio 3 Pro's screens unable to reach full brightness on laptop power. The page should tell the shopper to plug in the extender's power adapter, or a pass-through charger, to get the brightness on the spec sheet. Both sources disagree with treating a maker's 250–300 nit figure as what you get from one cable.

findings.label: Maximum brightness with the included power adapter
findings.source_title: Uperfect UStation Delta review: Portable monitor with dual 15.6-inch displays expands the desktop (Notebookcheck)
findings.note: Notebookcheck, Sebastian Bade, published 2023-08-20 (page modified 2026-10-05). Instrument: X-Rite i1Pro 2. Center/average: upper screen 212/200 cd/m², lower screen 195/182 cd/m². Notebookcheck: 'The maximum display brightness can only be achieved if connected to the included power adapter.'

findings.label: Maximum brightness on one USB-C cable (laptop power only)
findings.source_title: Uperfect UStation Delta review: Portable monitor with dual 15.6-inch displays expands the desktop (Notebookcheck)
findings.note: Notebookcheck: 'During single-cable operation via USB-C, we observed a maximum display brightness of only 160 cd/m².' 160 / 226 = 71%, so about 29% lower than with the adapter. The review also says one cable runs both screens and that no external supply is needed when USB-C carries both power and data.

findings.source_title: Uperfect UStation Delta review: Portable monitor with dual 15.6-inch displays expands the desktop (Notebookcheck)
findings.note: X-Rite i1Pro 2. DCI-P3 50.1% / 49.8%. Factory ColorChecker DeltaE 2000: 6.64 (upper), 4.92 (lower). The two panels in the same unit differ a lot in contrast.

findings.label: Brightness on laptop power (reviewer's observation, no number given)
findings.value: Below full brightness on laptop power alone; Macworld names no figure
findings.source_title: Mobile Pixels Trio 3 Pro review: MacBook's dual QHD screen wingspan (Macworld)
findings.note: Simon Jary, Macworld, 2026-04-02, tested on a 14-inch MacBook Pro: 'the Trio's screens can't draw enough power from the connected laptop to allow for maximum screen brightness.' The 300 nits in the review is Mobile Pixels' rating, not a measurement. Video path per the review: two USB-C cables; no driver if the laptop has two DP-enabled USB-C ports (quoting the manual); plain M1 and M2 MacBooks need Mobile Pixels' free software; M1/M2/M3 Pro/Max and M4/M5 MacBooks drive both screens without a driver.

findings.value: 258 cd/m² max, 235.3 cd/m² average; right screen 228 cd/m² center, 210 cd/m² average
findings.source_title: KYY X90A dual monitor review: The portable desktop expansion for laptops and tablets that features two displays (Notebookcheck)
findings.note: Notebookcheck, Sebastian Bade, published 2023-08-10. X-Rite i1Pro 2. sRGB 95.4% (left), 94.8% (right). This one is not driver-free: the box includes a 'USB stick (with display driver)' and both screens run from one USB-C cable. It serves as a measured example of a driver-based dual extender. I did not check whether it is still sold.
